title: Zelensky announces transfer of two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea
body:
On 23 September 2026, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced in an address to the UN General Assembly that Ukraine had transferred two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea, according to Reuters via The Korea Times. Ukraine had captured the two men in Russia's Kursk region in January 2025. They were the first North Korean soldiers taken alive since North Korea joined the war in 2024.

Zelensky had earlier said he would hand them to North Korean leader Kim Jong Un if that could help exchange them for Ukrainians held in Russia. Human rights groups urged sending them to South Korea, and South Korean media reported that the men wanted to defect. South Korean opposition lawmaker Yu Yong-weon said the men left Ukraine the previous weekend, passed through a third country and arrived in South Korea three to four days before his remarks on Thursday.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said it was deeply regrettable that Ukraine made the transfer public despite an agreement to keep it private. In June, South Korea had said it would accept any North Korean prisoners of war captured after fighting for Russia. North Korea has sent an estimated 14,000 to 15,000 troops to support Russia since 2024, mostly in Kursk.
